# pkgshift

> pkgshift is an open-source CLI for deterministic, transactional package manager and Bun-to-Deno runtime migrations in JavaScript repositories.

pkgshift supports npm, pnpm, Yarn Classic, Yarn Modern, Bun, vlt, and Deno dependency mode as production targets. `pkgshift doctor` returns a deterministic, non-ranking readiness matrix for every adapter from one repository scan; `--to <target>` narrows it to one target. Neither form creates a plan, persists state, executes a process, or changes the repository. A separate `pkgshift runtime to deno` surface applies permission-aware deterministic recipes for supported Bun application semantics without changing package-manager ownership. Managed `pkgshift skill` commands install the canonical portable Agent Skill for Codex or Claude Code through exact approval and protected ownership. The read-only `pkgshift explain` surface expands stable diagnostics and integrity-checks persisted package-manager or runtime plan, run, and verification evidence. The migration engine inspects the repository, creates an immutable plan, requires approval for that exact plan, applies the planned operations, verifies the result, and retains rollback artifacts. Coding agents operate the CLI; they do not author migration edits.

## Product

- [Project README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/README.md): Installation, CLI usage, package manager support, safety guarantees, and development commands.
- [Product vision](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/docs/product/vision.md): Product principles, user model, safety boundaries, and intended outcomes.
- [MVP status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/docs/product/mvp-status.md): Implemented capabilities, verification evidence, and current boundaries.
- [Capability matrix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/docs/support/capability-matrix.md): Support tiers and package-manager-specific behavior.

## Architecture

- [Migration engine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/docs/architecture/migration-engine.md): Inspect, plan, approve, apply, verify, and rollback pipeline.
- [Agent interface](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/docs/architecture/agent-interface.md): Machine-readable output, exit codes, next actions, and approval semantics.
- [Migration readiness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/docs/workflows/migration-readiness.md): Deterministic target assessment without a plan, state persistence, process execution, or repository writes.
- [Recovery and verification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/docs/architecture/recovery-and-verification.md): Snapshots, run journals, integrity checks, and rollback boundaries.
- [Bun-to-Deno runtime recipes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/docs/architecture/runtime-migration-recipes.md): Dedicated runtime recipe, permission, transaction, and residue-verification contract.

## Agent integration

- [Portable Agent Skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/skills/pkgshift/SKILL.md): Instructions for using pkgshift safely from compatible coding agents.
- [CLI contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/main/skills/pkgshift/references/cli-contract.md): Command shapes, structured responses, and exact approval flow.

## Distribution

- [Verified shell installer](https://bahadirarda.github.io/pkgshift/install.sh): Linux and macOS installer that verifies and transactionally activates the native release archive.
- [Verified PowerShell installer](https://bahadirarda.github.io/pkgshift/install.ps1): Windows x86-64 installer with the same checksum, metadata, Skill-data, smoke-check, and rollback contract.
- [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift/releases): Native binaries, checksums, release metadata, and build provenance.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/bahadirarda/pkgshift): Rust primary implementation, TypeScript reference, documentation, and release workflows.
